content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To care for a young rat, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Research reputable rat breeders or shelters (3 days)
Step 2. Purchase a large, multi-level wire cage (2 hours)
Step 3. Introduce the rat to its new cage environment (30 minutes)
Step 4. Buy high-quality rat blocks and supplemental grains (1 hour)
Step 5. Set up a consistent daily feeding schedule (10 minutes)
Step 6. Install a drip-bottle water system (15 minutes)
Step 7. Select safe, dust-free paper bedding (45 minutes)
Step 8. Place hidey-holes and fleece hammocks in the cage (20 minutes)
Step 9. Scatter-feed some seeds to encourage foraging (5 minutes)
Step 10. Purchase chew toys to manage tooth growth (30 minutes)
Step 11. Buy a digital scale to monitor growth (15 minutes)
Step 12. Find a local exotic veterinarian specializing in rodents (2 days)
Step 13. Perform a weekly deep clean of the cage pans (1 hour)
Step 14. Schedule an initial wellness checkup (1 week)
Step 15. Prepare a travel carrier for vet visits (20 minutes)
Step 16. Socialize the rat with gentle hand-feeding (30 minutes)
Step 17. Join an online rat care community for advice (1 hour)
Step 18. Set up a "rat-proofed" play area for out-of-cage time (2 hours)
Step 19. Buy a variety of healthy treats like peas and pasta (30 minutes)
Step 20. Install a solid-surface exercise wheel (10 minutes)
Step 21. Visit the breeder to pick out a healthy rat (2 hours)
Step 22. Budget for monthly food and medical expenses (1 hour)
Step 23. Bring the rat home in a secure box (1 hour)
Step 24. Learn about common respiratory symptoms in rats (4 hours)
Step 25. Purchase pet-safe disinfectant for cleaning (30 minutes)
Step 26. Set up a litter box for potty training (20 minutes)
Step 27. Buy a grooming brush for coat maintenance (15 minutes)
Step 28. Allow the rat to acclimate to your scent (2 days)
Step 29. Child-proof the electrical cords in the room (3 hours)
Step 30. Clear a dedicated space in the house for the cage (1 hour)
Step 31. Research toxic foods to avoid (2 hours)
Step 32. Handle the rat daily to build trust (30 minutes)
Step 33. Create a list of emergency vet contacts (30 minutes)
Step 34. Prepare a first-aid kit with saline and gauze (1 hour)
Step 35. Start a logbook of the rat’s weight and behavior (15 minutes)
Step 36. Quarantine the rat if you have other pets (2 weeks)
Step 37. Set up the base layer of bedding in the cage (15 minutes)
Step 38. Buy a specialized harness for supervised walks (45 minutes)
Step 39. Learn how to perform a "ratty health check" (1 hour)
Step 40. Decorate the cage with climbing ropes (30 minutes)
Step 41. Replace soiled bedding with fresh material (20 minutes)
Step 42. Purchase a mineral stone for gnawing (10 minutes)
Step 43. Measure out the first portion of lab blocks (5 minutes)
Step 44. Wash the food bowls with warm soapy water (10 minutes)
Step 45. Buy a thermometer to monitor room temperature (15 minutes)
Step 46. Stock up on paper towels for quick messes (10 minutes)
Step 47. Verify that the cage doors are securely latched (5 minutes)
Step 48. Set up the water bottle and check for leaks (10 minutes)
Step 49. Read a book on rat body language (5 hours)
Step 50. Double-check that the cage is away from drafts (10 minutes)
